questions.q: The Reservation buying type is available only for:
options: The Sales and Leads objectives with value tracking
The Awareness and Engagement objectives
The Traffic and App Promotion objectives on Facebook
All objectives, as long as the budget is lifetime
questions.explanation: Reservation only supports Awareness and Engagement. Sales, Leads, Traffic and App Promotion always run through Auction, no exceptions.

questions.q: The auction's total value is calculated as:
options: Advertiser bid × available budget + active placements
Bid strategy × promised frequency + estimated reach
Advertiser bid × estimated action rates + ad quality
Average CPM × expected CTR + historical CPC
questions.explanation: Total value = bid × estimated action rates + ad quality: your bid multiplied by the probability of action, plus ad quality. Cost control does NOT enter.

options: Daily, Lifetime, CBO, ABO and Bid Cap with a manual cap
Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads and Sales
Fixed CPM, target CPC, capped CPA, minimum ROAS and target CTR
Highest Volume, Highest Value, Cost per Result Goal, ROAS Goal, Bid Cap
questions.explanation: The 5 are: Highest Volume and Highest Value (spend-based), Cost per Result Goal and ROAS Goal (goal-based) and Bid Cap (manual). The rest are budgets or objectives.

questions.q: A client with a strict CPA cap who optimizes for volume of results:
options: Highest Volume, because it delivers the maximum results
Cost per Result Goal, which seeks volume while respecting the target cost
Highest Value, because it maximizes purchase value with the budget
ROAS Goal with a return target equivalent to the CPA
questions.explanation: Cost ceiling + volume optimization = Cost per Result Goal. Highest Volume respects no caps; Highest Value and ROAS Goal optimize value, not volume.

questions.q: When is Reservation better than Auction?
options: When you want the lowest possible cost per result
When the objective is Sales with a required minimum ROAS
When you need guaranteed reach and frequency at a fixed CPM
When the creative hasn't passed the ad review process yet
questions.explanation: Reservation buys certainty: reach and frequency locked at a fixed CPM, plannable in advance. Maximum efficiency and Sales live in Auction.

questions.q: An ecommerce demands a minimum ROAS of 4x optimizing for purchase value. Bid strategy?
options: Highest Value, which maximizes value without guaranteeing a return
Cost per Result Goal with a CPA equivalent to 25%
Bid Cap with a cap equal to the store's average ticket
ROAS Goal with a 4x target (requires value tracking)
questions.explanation: There's a required minimum return: ROAS Goal targets that multiple. Highest Value maximizes value but doesn't commit to a specific return.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT enter the auction's total value?
options: The advertiser bid you declare
The estimated action rates for that person at that moment
The cost control of the chosen bid strategy
The ad quality based on user signals
questions.explanation: Total value has exactly 3 components: bid, estimated action rates and ad quality. The bid strategy controls how you spend, not how the auction is won.

questions.q: A brand must appear on an exact day with reach committed to leadership, no cost surprises:
options: Reservation: delivery and CPM locked in advance
Auction + Highest Volume with a high budget that day
Auction + Bid Cap with an aggressive cap to win auctions
Auction + Cost per Result Goal with an hourly schedule
questions.explanation: Certainty of date, reach and cost = Reservation. In Auction the price floats with demand and nothing guarantees a specific day's delivery.

questions.q: Raising the bid to the max 'to win every auction' is inefficient because:
options: A high bid lowers the ad's estimated action rates
The auction discards bids above the category average for the business
Cost goes up but delivery freezes in the learning phase
The highest total value wins; improving creative and relevance beats overpaying
questions.explanation: The winner has the highest total value (bid × action rates + quality). Improving creative and relevance moves 2 of the 3 components without inflating cost.

questions.q: Bid Cap differs from Cost per Result Goal in that:
options: Bid Cap limits the bid per auction; Cost per Result Goal targets an average cost per result
Bid Cap guarantees the final cost per result; Cost per Result Goal only limits the bid per auction
Bid Cap is exclusive to Reservation; Cost per Result Goal to Auction
Bid Cap optimizes for value; Cost per Result Goal for volume without caps
questions.explanation: Bid Cap is manual control of the max bid per auction (not the final CPA). Cost per Result Goal lets the system seek volume around a target cost.
